chunks: When you stand in prayer for the people,
do not be one who causes boredom nor one who is wasteful, for among the people there is the sick and those who have needs.
And I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when he sent me to Yemen, 'How should I lead them in prayer?'
He replied, 'Lead them in prayer as the weakest of them would pray, and be merciful to the believers.'

key_terms.أَضْعَفِهِمْ: The weakest of them (in terms of prayer ability or endurance)
key_terms.مُضَيِّعاً: One who is wasteful or hasty
key_terms.مُنَفِّراً: One who causes boredom or annoyance

ai.seo_question: How should a leader conduct congregational prayer according to Imam Ali's instructions?
ai.summary: This directive, delivered during Imam Ali’s appointment of Malik al-Ashtar as governor of Egypt, underscores the principle of *khushu'* and consideration for the *muqaddam* (leader) to adapt to the *muqtadi* (congregation). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the leader’s humility and mercy, ensuring that prayer serves as a source of comfort rather than burden, particularly for the sick and those with urgent needs. This practice aligns with the Prophetic tradition of leading with the weakest member in mind, reinforcing the social responsibility of religious leadership.

en.sayed-ali-raza: When you lead the prayers for the people
it should be neither (too long as to be) boring nor (too short as to be) wasteful, because among the people there are the sick as well as those who have needs of their own.
When the Messenger of Allāh (S) sent me to Yemen I enquired how I should offer prayers with them
and he replied, “Say the prayers as the weakest of them would say, and be considerate to the believers.”
